{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjdzc8AAAABbwzsgA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IVzhFUaFE", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3IV", "number": 95, "title": "Support standard Saturn disc images (including CHD) without mandatory emulator-specific sidecar files", "body": "## Problem

The browser's media picker currently accepts cooked 2048-byte-sector ISO images or CUE files with all referenced BINARY track files. It does **not** accept CHD. Users with otherwise standard CD images must therefore convert/extract a CHD before using this emulator, even when the media contains all necessary tracks. The project also exposes an original `.srw` / `SRW1` subchannel companion format (selected through `REM SATURN_RW`), which is valuable for focused tests but must never become a prerequisite for ordinary disc loading.

The goal is to align user-supplied media requirements with normal Sega Saturn emulation: no mandatory emulator-specific manifest, extracted executable, patched/rebuilt disc, sidecar, or per-title metadata. Distinguish files that *constitute* the original medium (such as CUE and its referenced BIN tracks), optional user-supplied BIOS firmware, and genuinely required physical accessories from invented emulator-specific requirements. **Media format support is distinct from retail-game runtime/BIOS/hardware compatibility**; do not claim commercial titles run merely because an image mounts.

Checked `main`: `66ef66a00e8c55194e5bf96b123cada0003d4c8f` (2026-11-02).

## Expected outcome

A user can select a supported standalone `.chd`, a cooked `.iso`, or a normal `.cue` together with its referenced `.bin` file(s) and mount/run it in the existing HLE-disc or user-provided-BIOS paths **without making or supplying a second, emulator-specific data file**. Keep the original built-in homebrew demos working. A BIOS is still optional in HLE mode and must be provided locally when choosing genuine-BIOS mode; no bundled/downloaded proprietary assets.

In particular, support ordinary **self-contained MAME CHD v5 CD-ROM images** produced by `chdman createcd`, including representative data and mixed data/audio discs, with track metadata, pregaps/indexes, sector types, and CD-DA preserved as supported by the existing media/CD model. Do not depend on running `chdman`, another external program, a server, or a conversion step at runtime. Explicitly report unsupported CHD variants/codecs or parent/differencing CHDs rather than silently accepting a damaged interpretation or asking for a nonstandard sidecar.

## Context and reproduction

- `web/index.html` media input accepts `.iso,.cue,.bin,.srw`; `web/app.js` accepts only 2048-byte-sector standalone ISO or CUE + BINARY track selections, reads selected bytes into Wasm, and has no CHD dispatch.
- `src/disc.rs`, `src/media.rs`, `src/cd.rs`, `src/cd_rw.rs`, and `src/wasm.rs` already implement sector-addressed boot/runtime media, mixed-mode CUE, CD-DA, selected R–W subcode, and HLE/external-BIOS media paths. **Reuse** the existing media semantics instead of creating a second boot/CD behavior.
- `docs/cd-rw.md` defines the explicitly optional original `SRW1` companion: a CUE's `REM SATURN_RW "file.srw"` resolves supplied bytes, whereas ordinary ISO/CUE/BIN without that directive do not need one. Preserve this advanced/diagnostic path without treating SRW1 as a normal user prerequisite.
- `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/setup.md`, `homebrew/star-collector`, `homebrew/prism-courier` and `homebrew/hardware-lab` document existing media limits, demos and tests.
- Upstream format reference: [MAME chdman documentation](https://docs.mamedev.org/tools/chdman.html) (CD creation/extraction and compression), [CHD/CD track metadata definitions](https://github.com/mamedev/mame/blob/master/src/lib/util/chd.cpp). Validate CHD track layout and supported codecs against the actual format, not filename/extension alone.
- Reproduction today: select a self-contained, valid CHD CD image using the local file picker. It is not recognized as a supported media type. Reproduction uses independently authored, redistributable test media; proprietary commercial images are not required.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] **Media input contract:** document the supported formats and when each file is needed. For an ordinary disc, accept one supported standalone CHD, one cooked ISO, or one CUE plus only its actual referenced track files. Neither HLE nor external-BIOS mode may require a private manifest, pre-extracted `GAME.BIN`, patched boot ISO, game-specific JSON/database, `.srw`, `.sub`, or extra BIOS-like assets to *mount* otherwise supported media. Retain the existing local-only/opt-in BIOS policy. Clearly distinguish *mounting* from *successfully booting a retail game*.
- [ ] **CHD v5 CD-ROM reader:** implement a self-contained CHD input path usable in production native Rust/Wasm/browser (not a test-only decoder). Support representative data-only and mixed data/audio CHD generated from original licensed fixtures using common `chdman createcd` CD codecs; retain track numbers, data/audio types, pregap/index/leadout and actual readable sector bytes to the extent encoded and supported. State the tested codec/layout inventory; reject unsupported versions, parent-backed images, metadata, compression or malformed sizes with actionable errors. Do not invent audio or subcode bytes.
- [ ] **Integrate with the current CD/boot semantics:** use the same underlying `Media`/sector reader and existing boot modes, including real FIFO/SCU-DMA/IRQ/CD-DA behavior. Loading CHD must not depend on host-side game-name checks, new per-game boot rules, private library interception or altered HLE/BIOS selection.
- [ ] **No extra conversion or sidecar:** use the chosen CHD itself at runtime without asking the user to pre-expand it to BIN/CUE or install/run `chdman`. Avoid writing an expanded copy to browser storage or filesystem. Bound decompression/caching and protect against excessive memory use, malformed headers, integer overflow, and decompression bombs. No CDN, server, analytics, upload, or external binary dependency in the Play app. Evaluate a suitable licensed decoder and record the dependency/license/runtime tradeoffs.
- [ ] **Keep optional SRW1 behavior exceptional:** existing `REM SATURN_RW` tests continue to work only when explicitly requested; ordinary CHD/ISO/CUE loading never requires SRW1. Where a normal format encodes supported subchannel information, consume it directly when feasible; otherwise preserve existing no-subchannel behavior and document the limitation rather than fabricate data or impose a companion file.
- [ ] **UI and error handling:** update picker labels/accept filter/validation and help text for CHD, ISO and CUE/BIN. Missing referenced CUE tracks, incorrectly supplied lone raw BIN, malformed CHD, unsupported parent/codec and exceeding resource bounds must produce clear errors, with no stale media, unintended HLE fallback or partial changed machine state beyond established failed-load semantics. Switching modes, cancellation, Reset/Restart and retained-media behavior remain correct.
- [ ] **Independent equivalence tests:** build at least two small original, redistributable disc fixtures (one data-only and one mixed-mode with CD-DA), compare complete logical sector/track/TOC and representative CD commands, data/FIFO/DMA and audio outputs between CHD and the corresponding ISO/CUE-BIN media. Include mutated content, pregap/index boundaries where present, malformed/truncated/corrupt CHDs and a no-SRW1 ordinary-disc case. Exercise native and production Wasm/Chromium at `/saturn-rust/` with the same substantive oracles; preserve Star Collector, Prism Courier, Hardware Lab, existing ISO/CUE/BIN and optional SRW1 regressions.
- [ ] **Reproducible build and CI:** generated fixtures are original/licensed and reproducible; CI must not download proprietary firmware/discs or depend on a user's own files. Run applicable Rust format/build/tests/Clippy, Wasm build/Clippy, fixture validation and complete browser tests with no skipped existing coverage. Report actual commands/results, errors, and any memory/performance impact, following `docs/development-flow.md` and `docs/ci-performance.md`.
- [ ] **Documentation:** update README, architecture, setup, and media docs with what loads, what cannot, how to select multi-file CUE, the distinction between optional BIOS and disc content, the diagnostic SRW1 exception, codec/version/size limits, and the fact that image-format support alone does not establish commercial-game compatibility.

## Optional validation / separate future work

- Optional `.m3u` multi-disc playlists (not required to load each disc); additional CloneCD `.ccd/.img/.sub` and `.mds/.mdf` layouts; less-common/older CHD codecs and versions; special physical cartridge ROM/RAM accessories; broader HLE/retail BIOS and CD-library compatibility. These are **not** mandatory for this Issue and must not be introduced as a condition for standard CHD/CUE/ISO support.
- Physical consoles and personally supplied BIOS/commercial games are not needed to complete or validate this task.

## Required post-merge verification

None. Verify functionality before merge via native/Wasm/Chromium CI; live Pages inspection is not a gate.
